Everyone is talking about the AI 'race'. But races aren't won in the first corner. They're won in the final sprint - and over the very last mile. And the last mile is something that the Global South knows very well.

Far from being left out or left behind, the Global South could set the pace for global AI direction. And we're working with governments around the world to prepare them for what we see as the crucial AI 'sprint' - in particular, how countries can position energy and AI as crucial catalysts for growth. With these two revolutions having the potential to become definitive inflection points for 21st century sustainable development. 

We've identified a 'Green Window of Opportunity' where decision-makers, policymakers, and innovators can leverage the combined potential of energy and AI to chart a new pathway. Some of the areas we're driving exploration around include:

🤝 How to build locally-owned and locally-relevant domestic AI–energy innovation ecosystems anchored in local talent, universities, businesses, and public institutions.

🏛️ The need to make 'Green AI' THE critical pathway through supportive regulation, infrastructure planning, and investment incentives - with the potential for this to become an area of national comparative advantage.

⬆️ Identifying how countries and communities can move up the clean energy, critical mineral, and digital value chains to retain greater economic value domestically - and how they can build crucial and cumulative energy, AI, and development gains.

⚡ How countries can shape and support AI and clean-energy entrepreneurs through targeted finance, incubation, market creation, and skills development.

We are not about abstract discussions of technology, status quo energy policy, or generic policy recommendations. We really do see an important moment for development in the coming months and years. Countries sitting at the intersection of renewable energy - many of which are in the Global South - and AI explorations (with countries across Latin America, Africa, and Asia-Pacific moving quickly) could reap an unprecedented digital development dividend. Get in touch if you want to explore what the AI and energy revolutions could mean for your country.

➡️ More in our recent UNDP paper with the TIDE Centre, University of Oxford : The Energy Sprint of the AI Race: A Green Window of Opportunity for Developing Countries?
